inclusion.I2: Human participants performing an emotion regulation or reappraisal task, broadly defined.
inclusion.I3: Includes at least one group of healthy adults.

exclusion.E1: Non-empirical papers (e.g., reviews, meta-analyses) without original human data.
exclusion.E2: Doesn't include at least one healthy adult sample.

inclusion.I6: fMRI Task- reappraisal of positive and negative emotions as emotion regulation strategy using up- and down-regulation of emotions as the regulation goal
inclusion.I7: Target sample- at least one group of healthy adults with no prior report of neurological, medical, or psychiatric disorders
inclusion.I8: Analysis- Reports at least one within-task contrast related to emotion regulation (e.g., “reappraise > look”, “down-regulate > maintain”, “up-regulate > maintain”) for the target sample.
inclusion.I9: Whole-brain evidence- The target analysis must be a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map
inclusion.I10: It is acceptable for qualifying whole-brain results to be reported in tables of coordinates, figures, or supplementary materials, as long as they are clearly described in the text.

exclusion.E3: Non-empirical papers (e.g., reviews, meta-analyses, methods-only, simulations) without original fMRI data in healthy adults.
exclusion.E4: Studies that report only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses or only report small-volume corrected results without an accompanying whole-brain map.
exclusion.E5: Studies that report only seed-based connectivity, effective connectivity (e.g., PPI, DCM), or resting-state analyses (e.g., ICA, PLE, Hurst exponents) without also reporting a whole-brain task activation map.
exclusion.E6: Studies that report only between-group contrasts or interactions (e.g., subgroup vs subgroup, patient vs control)
